report.verdict: Your B2B marketing work and tool list are relevant to Tallgrass Health Software. I’d hesitate to move this forward for Marketing Operations Coordinator because the resume doesn’t yet show how you’ve used HubSpot or run campaigns on deadline.
write_up: You’ve moved from event and sales support at Keystone Benefits Group to newsletters, webinars, content planning and reporting at Brightfield Software. It’s common for a coordinator resume to list the work this way, but yours won’t stand out in a pile for Tallgrass while your part in the campaigns and the tools you used are mostly left unstated.

The LinkedIn and blog calendar line is your best model: it names what you managed and where the content went. Your B2B background and the tools in your skills section give the application a useful starting point, but a recruiter can’t connect HubSpot to the work yet.

Let’s start with the Brightfield newsletter and webinar lines. Add the parts you handled, then connect your reporting work to the tools and campaign measures you used, where you can. Those details will also help show how your experience fits a marketing operations role.

cards.line: Coordinated the monthly customer newsletter and product announcement emails
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the emails were yours to coordinate, but not which parts you handled or how large the audience was. Those details matter for a job centered on email campaigns.
cards.example: Coordinated the monthly customer newsletter and product announcement emails for [audience size] by [your contribution]
cards.question: Which parts of the emails did you handle, and how large was the audience?

cards.line: Supported webinar planning with the product marketing team
cards.cannot_tell: Planning could mean several things. Tallgrass needs support from registration through follow-up, so name the parts you worked on.
cards.example: Supported webinar planning with the product marketing team by [your contribution]
cards.question: What did you handle in planning the webinars?

cards.line: Managed the content calendar for LinkedIn and the company blog
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model for naming both the thing you owned and the channels it served.

cards.line: Pulled weekly campaign reports for the marketing manager
cards.cannot_tell: The weekly cadence is useful, but the reports could cover almost anything. The measures and tools would show how your reporting relates to the Tallgrass job.
cards.example: Pulled weekly campaign reports on [metrics] in [tool] for the marketing manager
cards.question: Which measures did you report on, and which tool did you use?

cards.line: Helped prepare slide decks and one-pagers for the sales team
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the deliverables, but not what you contributed to them or what they covered.
cards.example: Helped prepare slide decks and one-pagers on [subject] for the sales team by [your contribution]
cards.question: What did you contribute to the decks and one-pagers, and what were they about?

cards.line: Kept the brand asset library organized
cards.cannot_tell: This leaves the work behind the library unstated. A little detail would show what you maintained.
cards.example: Kept the brand asset library organized by [your contribution]
cards.question: What did you do to keep the brand asset library organized?

fit.why: Your headline and current role both name Marketing Coordinator, and your work covers newsletters, webinars, content and reporting.
fit.level: mid-level, current coordinator role with an earlier marketing assistant role
fit.note: Your webinar support and campaign reporting are relevant to the Tallgrass role. Connect those activities to the tools you used where you can. The job is hybrid in Columbus.
